about-spherex.content.5.label: SPHEREx is NASA’s space observatory designed to explore the universe in more than 100 wavelengths of infrared light. By

fields.text:
NASA's SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer) is a space-based observatory conducting an all-sky spectral survey across 102 near-infrared wavelength bands, covering 0.75 to 5.0 micrometres.

By mapping the entire sky, SPHEREx helps scientists investigate the origins of the universe, understand how galaxies form and evolve, and explore the distribution of water and other essential ingredients for life throughout our galaxy.

fields.text: "SPHEREx is helping scientists build a detailed picture of the cosmos by collecting infrared data across the entire sky. Its observations provide valuable insights into how the universe evolved and where the ingredients for life may be found".

details.content.9.label: The Solar System formed about 4.6 billion years ago from a cloud of gas and dust. Gravity drew much of that material tow

fields.text: The Solar System formed about 4.6 billion years ago from a cloud of gas and dust. Gravity drew much of that material toward the young Sun, while the remaining matter gradually formed planets, moons, asteroids and comets. Each of these objects preserves clues about the earliest stages of our cosmic neighborhood.

details.content.10.label: The four inner planets—Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars—have solid, rocky surfaces, but their environments are dramaticall

fields.text: The four inner planets—Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars—have solid, rocky surfaces, but their environments are dramatically different. Comparing them helps scientists understand how a planet’s size, atmosphere and distance from the Sun influence its history.

details.content.12.label: Farther out are the giant planets. Jupiter and Saturn are rich in hydrogen and helium, while Uranus and Neptune contain

fields.text: Farther out are the giant planets. Jupiter and Saturn are rich in hydrogen and helium, while Uranus and Neptune contain larger proportions of heavier substances. Their rings, storms and complex systems of moons make them fascinating targets for observation.

details.content.15.label: A planet is only part of the story. Moons can have underground oceans, active geology or icy surfaces that respond to th

fields.text: A planet is only part of the story. Moons can have underground oceans, active geology or icy surfaces that respond to their parent planet’s gravitational pull. Studying these worlds helps researchers ask where water and other essential ingredients can exist.

details.content.16.label: Venus and Mars also show how planetary atmospheres can change over time. Venus has an exceptionally dense atmosphere, wh

fields.text: Venus and Mars also show how planetary atmospheres can change over time. Venus has an exceptionally dense atmosphere, while Mars has a much thinner one. Their contrasting conditions help place Earth’s environment in a wider scientific context.

details.content.17.label: Small bodies carry information about the Solar System’s past. Asteroids are rocky remnants from early planet formation,

fields.text: Small bodies carry information about the Solar System’s past. Asteroids are rocky remnants from early planet formation, while comets contain ice and dust that can become visible as they approach the Sun.

details.content.18.label: Each world in the Solar System offers a different clue about how planets form and evolve.

fields.text: Each world in the Solar System offers a different clue about how planets form and evolve.

details.content.19.label: Beyond Neptune lies a broad region of icy objects known as the Kuiper Belt. Pluto is one of its best-known members and i

fields.text: Beyond Neptune lies a broad region of icy objects known as the Kuiper Belt. Pluto is one of its best-known members and is classified as a dwarf planet. This distant region demonstrates that the Solar System extends far beyond the eight major planets.

details.content.21.label: New observations continue to challenge familiar textbook images. Robotic probes explore planets and moons up close, whil

fields.text: New observations continue to challenge familiar textbook images. Robotic probes explore planets and moons up close, while ground-based and space telescopes monitor atmospheres, surfaces and the changing positions of small bodies.

details.content.24.label: An observation becomes more meaningful when researchers compare data from different wavelengths. Visible and infrared vi

fields.text: An observation becomes more meaningful when researchers compare data from different wavelengths. Visible and infrared views, for example, can highlight different physical processes and make otherwise difficult-to-see structures easier to study.

details.content.25.label: For curious sky watchers, the best starting point is to ask questions, compare reliable evidence and revisit a familiar

fields.text: For curious sky watchers, the best starting point is to ask questions, compare reliable evidence and revisit a familiar world with fresh information. The Solar System is not a finished chapter: it is an active area of scientific discovery.

fields.text: SPHEREx is NASA’s all-sky infrared survey mission that maps the entire sky across 102 infrared colors. Our platform transforms these scientific observations into an interactive virtual telescope, allowing users to explore the infrared universe from anywhere. Users can navigate the sky, search for Detector arrays, switch between infrared wavelengths, and examine stars, galaxies, nebulae, and other cosmic phenomena. By making complex astronomical data visual, interactive, and accessible, the platform helps students, researchers, and astronomy enthusiasts understand the hidden features of spherex mission and discover objects that cannot be easily seen using visible light.

observatory.content.40.label: We believe that looking at the stars is more than simply observing distant objects. It is an opportunity to understand w

fields.text:
NASA's SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer) is a space-based infrared observatory designed to conduct an unprecedented all-sky spectral survey.

By observing the universe in 102 different infrared wavelength bands, SPHEREx helps scientists investigate the origins and evolution of galaxies, study the history of cosmic structures and identify water and organic molecules in regions where stars and planetary systems form.

Through NightLock, we bring these scientific concepts closer to everyone with interactive visualisations, educational resources and an accessible digital exploration experience.
